title: Cognitive Changes in Parkinson's
content: Parkinson's disease can affect cognition, including thinking, memory, attention, planning, problem-solving and the ability to process information. Cognitive changes vary between individuals and may range from mild difficulties to more significant impairment. A person may experience slower thinking, difficulty concentrating or paying attention, problems with planning and completing tasks, difficulty finding words, or changes in memory. Memory or thinking difficulties can have many causes and do not by themselves establish that a person has Parkinson's disease. New or worsening cognitive problems should be discussed with a healthcare professional so that possible causes can be properly assessed.
